name: Future Artificial Intelligence Co. (شركة المستقبل للذكاء الاصطناعي), trading as HUMAIN (هيوماين)
employees: Not disclosed; 'over 120 AI specialists, including 35 PhD holders' on the ALLaM model team (SPA, Aug 2025)

ownership.notes: Launched on 12 May 2025 as 'a PIF-owned company' chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; its releases still describe it as 'a PIF company' through September 2026. On 28 Oct 2025 PIF and Aramco signed a non-binding term sheet for Aramco to acquire 'a significant minority stake', with PIF retaining the majority, and the PIF-owned Saudi Company for Artificial Intelligence (SCAI) was transferred into HUMAIN. Argaam reports the European Commission cleared the 'joint acquisition of HUMAIN by Saudi Aramco and the Public Investment Fund' (23 Jul 2026). No completion has been announced. The legal name appears in Al Moammar Information Systems' Tadawul disclosures; no commercial-registration number was found. Semafor (8 Sep 2026) reports IPO preparation for a listing in Riyadh and New York by 2029.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: HUMAIN is Saudi Arabia's state AI company, owned by PIF. It sells GPU capacity to labs and platforms — xAI, Together AI, Adobe, Luma and an AWS 'AI Zone' — and it is the party that signs for the kingdom's AI data-centre power. On the record it signed a National Grid SA supply agreement for a Riyadh AI data-centre project (2 Sep 2026). Trade press reports it tendered the high-voltage infrastructure of a 6 GW Al-Saad campus in east Riyadh. On 20 Sep 2026 it signed a 250 MW engineering-procurement-construction agreement with Al Moammar Information Systems (MIS), worth about SAR 8.76B and executed through HUMAIN-issued work orders. No power-equipment supplier to HUMAIN is named in any source. Its targets are gigawatt-scale: 1.9 GW by 2030 and about 6 GW by 2034 in CEO statements. Energised capacity is small: the only operating figure is its own NVIDIA cloud, launched at 1.1 MW, relayed from its LEAP 2026 disclosures, plus an AMD MI355X cluster live since 31 Aug 2026 with no MW stated. BACKGROUND: Launched 12 May 2025 and chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. CEO Tareq Amin, formerly of Aramco Digital and Rakuten Mobile. Its main commitments: NVIDIA (18,000 GB300 first, up to 600,000 GPUs over three years in Saudi Arabia and the US), AMD and Cisco (a joint venture targeting up to 1 GW by 2030), a US$3B investment in xAI now held as SpaceX shares, and its own models (ALLaM; humain-m3, built by the Chinese company MiniMax). It publishes no revenue, and the US has licensed it up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips. SemiAnalysis lists it 'Unavailable' in ClusterMAX 3.0 because HUMAIN never responded to its request to test.
ecosystemRole: We assess HUMAIN as the corpus's first sovereign neocloud. It is a state-owned builder and seller of AI compute whose tenants are foreign labs and platforms, and it is the owner-of-record behind Saudi Arabia's AI data-centre power demand. Basis: its launch mandate was to 'streamline various data center initiatives, procure hardware'. AMD's 2025 release says 'HUMAIN will oversee end-to-end delivery, including hyperscale data center, sustainable power systems'. It is the grid counterparty to National Grid SA and the owner that appoints MIS as its engineering-procurement-construction contractor. For a power-equipment seller the door is two-step: the EPC contractor buys, against designs and work orders HUMAIN approves. On partner-led campuses — DataVolt at Oxagon, AirTrunk, the AWS AI Zone — the partner buys instead. It is not a hyperscaler on the record: its own cloud and models are small beside the capacity it builds and lets to others.

productsAndServices.name: AI data centres — owned builds and partner campuses
productsAndServices.category: AI data-centre development (owner and grid counterparty)
productsAndServices.description: HUMAIN develops capacity by three routes. (1) Owner-built: MIS designs and builds a private AI data centre for HUMAIN. It began as a 50 MW, 12-month design-build contract of about SAR 1.88B (signed 5 Mar 2026) and was expanded to 250 MW through an EPC agreement signed 20 Sep 2026, worth over 689% of MIS's 2025 revenue (about SAR 8.76B). That agreement is 'carried out under work orders issued by HUMAIN' and supersedes the March contract. MIS's filings name no site. (2) The Al-Saad campus in east Riyadh: MEED describes a 24 km² site of six 1 GW plots. HUMAIN tendered its infrastructure on an early-contractor-involvement basis, and Construction Review reports Al-Yamama selected. The Saudi Press Agency calls it an AI data centre 'with a capacity of up to 6 gigawatts'. (3) Partner-led: DataVolt is building HUMAIN's 100 MW inside its Oxagon (NEOM) campus for 2028; AirTrunk (Blackstone) 'will lead development' of a campus of about US$3B; AWS 'will deploy and manage' GPUs in an AI Zone; and an stc/center3 joint venture of up to 1 GW is still a memorandum of understanding. HUMAIN also leases capacity: it rents colocation from MIS (SAR 51.23M over 60 months, with a second award of about SAR 382M).
highlights: Grid: 'The first agreement, signed by National Grid SA and HUMAIN, covers the provision of electricity to the AI data centers project in Riyadh' (SPA, 2 Sep 2026); no MW or date disclosed

Al-Saad scope as tendered: '380kV/132kV/33kV electrical distribution network, two substations with a capacity of 500MVA and 200MVA, bulk supply point (2,000MVA)'; client advisers Hatch, Egis and JLL (MEED)
Stated design philosophy: 'robotic, modular, and optimized for the lowest total cost of ownership' (homepage, archived March 2026)

Targets: '1.9 gigawatts … by 2030 and over 6 GW by 2034' (Fortune, CEO statements); Middle East AI News relays HUMAIN saying Al-Saad's first phase 'will deliver 1GW of capacity by or in 2027', while the NYT (via Startup Fortune) reports 250 MW by the start of 2027 — not reconciled
Energised: HUMAIN's NVIDIA cloud 'launched … with 1.1 megawatts running', targeting 35.1 MW by 2027 (Global Data Center Hub, from LEAP 2026 disclosures)
productsAndServices.positioning: Low-cost Saudi power and land as the offer: xAI's release credits 'HUMAIN's low-cost value proposition in infrastructure design, construction, and operations'; Together AI calls Saudi power capacity 'a key advantage'
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owner-appointed EPC contractors (MIS) for its own builds; partner-developer structures (DataVolt, AirTrunk, AWS) where the partner designs, finances and operates
productsAndServices.roadmap: MIS work orders to be announced as issued; Al-Saad phase 1 claimed for 2027; AMD/Cisco 250 MW from 2027; DataVolt Oxagon 100 MW in 2028; AWS AI Zone up to 50 MW by 2028

productsAndServices.name: Compute and cloud — GPU-as-a-service and capacity partnerships
productsAndServices.description: HUMAIN sells compute from its capacity to others. The AMD and Cisco systems that went live on 31 Aug 2026 'enabl[e] HUMAIN to offer GPU-as-a-service across a wide range of use cases, from model training to inferencing', on AMD Instinct MI355X with Cisco networking. With NVIDIA, the first phase was 18,000 GB300 (May 2025), expanded to 'up to 600,000' NVIDIA GPUs over three years in Saudi Arabia and the United States (Nov 2025). Named compute customers and partners: xAI (a framework for a flagship '500 MW+' facility that HUMAIN designs, builds and operates), Together AI (a new 250 MW data centre plus 55 MW of dedicated capacity, which Together resells to its customers), Adobe ('HUMAIN's first global AI data center customer'), Luma, Reflection AI and Cohere. Developer access runs through HUMAIN Node, an OpenAI-compatible model API. HUMAIN ONE's models run 'on Groq's ultra-fast inference infrastructure, hosted in Dammam'. Qualcomm AI200/AI250 inference racks are targeted at 200 MW 'starting in 2026'.
highlights: CEO (Aug 2025): 'HUMAIN currently serves 130 international clients, with Saudi Arabia accounting for just 1% of usage' (Argaam interview)
Together AI: the partnership is 'expected to yield over $5 billion in gross annualized revenue in its first year' — a projection for an unbuilt facility, shared through a revenue-sharing arrangement
AMD/Cisco/HUMAIN joint venture: up to 1 GW by 2030; next phase up to 250 MW on AMD Instinct MI400 from 2027
SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX 3.0 (23 Sep 2026): listed 'Not Recommended – Unavailable' because 'we have yet to get a response from the team'
productsAndServices.positioning: A sovereign, export-oriented neocloud: SemiAnalysis covers it in the neocloud universe but has not tested it; its direct Gulf rival is G42's Core42, which holds a stronger US export position
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct capacity partnerships; revenue-share resale through Together AI; hyperscaler-operated zones (AWS); HUMAIN Node API
productsAndServices.roadmap: xAI's flagship to start at 50 MW and expand to 500 MW (Communications Minister, LEAP 2026); Cohere 'at least 50 megawatts' by Q4 2027 (Middle East AI News)

productsAndServices.name: Models — ALLaM, humain-m3 and HUMAIN Chat
productsAndServices.description: ALLaM 34B is 'HUMAIN's flagship Arabic large language model', built on models from SDAIA's National Center for AI. It powers HUMAIN Chat, launched on 25 Aug 2025 and 'hosted end-to-end on HUMAIN infrastructure in the Kingdom', and is to be offered on Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry. humain-m3, a 428-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, was 'commissioned by HUMAIN and delivered by MiniMax' and released in research preview on HUMAIN Node on 3 Sep 2026.
highlights: humain-m3: Startup Fortune reports HUMAIN 'initially presented it as a homegrown model until users matched its parameters exactly to MiniMax's, forcing a public clarification'
ALLaM team: 'over 120 AI specialists, including 35 PhD holders' (SPA)
productsAndServices.positioning: Arabic-first sovereign models; the model layer is small beside the infrastructure business
productsAndServices.soldThrough: HUMAIN Chat app; HUMAIN Node API; Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry
productsAndServices.roadmap: humain-m3 open weights under the MiniMax Community License targeted for about October 2026 (company)

productsAndServices.name: HUMAIN ONE, enterprise software and devices
productsAndServices.category: Enterprise AI software, services and AI PCs
productsAndServices.description: HUMAIN ONE is an 'agentic AI operating system' launched at FII9 on 28 Oct 2025. It is sold on AWS Marketplace and bundled with Microsoft 365 Copilot on Azure (target: one million users across the Middle East and Africa). Around it: HUMAIN OS (an AI-native Linux, with KORA Systems), the HUMAIN Fabric data platform (with MinIO), AI PCs (Horizon Pro on Snapdragon X Elite; a Windows-based HUMAIN AI PC from 20 Sep 2026), autonomous trucking with Applied Intuition, consulting with Microsoft, Accenture and McKinsey, and framework agreements with the Ministries of Interior, Justice and Communications and with SDAIA.
highlights: Government customers: Ministry of Interior (HUMAIN Chat for personnel via Absher, Dec 2025), SDAIA (Jan 2026), MCIT and the Ministry of Justice (Sep 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: Full-stack: 'We build the entire AI stack: data centers, cloud, models, and applications' (homepage)
targetSegments: enterprises in the Middle East and Africa
productsAndServices.roadmap: HUMAIN AI PC target of one million units across the Middle East and Africa by 2030 (company)

productsAndServices.name: Investments — xAI, Luma and the venture programme
productsAndServices.description: HUMAIN invested US$3B in xAI's Series E 'just prior to its acquisition by SpaceX', became 'a significant minority shareholder', and its holdings 'subsequently converted into shares in SpaceX' (18 Feb 2026). Reuters reports HUMAIN led Luma AI's US$900M Series C (Nov 2025); Luma is the reported anchor of the AMD/Cisco joint venture's first 100 MW. Trade press reports a US$10B 'HUMAIN Ventures' fund, which no first-party source was found to confirm.
highlights: Customers funded by HUMAIN buy HUMAIN capacity: xAI (equity, then a 500 MW+ framework) and Luma (equity, then the joint venture's first 100 MW)
productsAndServices.positioning: CEO Tareq Amin (Fortune): 'We don't do passive investments' — the fund invests only in companies committing to Saudi compute or a Saudi workforce
targetSegments: AI labs and AI-native companies that will use Saudi compute
productsAndServices.roadmap: Amin says the venture fund could launch 'at an even larger scale by the end of 2026' (Fortune)

relationships.scale: up to US$10B / 500 MW over five years; joint venture up to 1 GW by 2030
relationships.via: AMD Instinct MI355X; MI400 Series from 2027
relationships.note: AMD supplies the GPUs behind HUMAIN's first live GPU-as-a-service capacity, through a joint venture with Cisco in which HUMAIN supplies the data-centre capacity.
relationships.context:
May 2025: AMD and HUMAIN agreed that 'the parties will invest up to $10B to deploy 500 megawatts of AI compute capacity over the next five years', with HUMAIN to 'oversee end-to-end delivery, including hyperscale data center, sustainable power systems, and global fiber interconnects'.

November 2025: AMD, Cisco and HUMAIN formed a joint venture targeting up to 1 GW by 2030, with a first phase of 100 MW. Reuters reports Luma AI contracted that entire first phase.

31 August 2026: MI355X systems went live, 'enabling HUMAIN to offer GPU-as-a-service', with the next phase of up to 250 MW on MI400 Series from 2027. The joint venture's legal entity and equity split are not disclosed.

relationships.scale: 18,000 GB300 first phase; up to 600,000 GPUs over three years (Saudi Arabia and the US)
relationships.via: GB300 Grace Blackwell with NVIDIA InfiniBand
relationships.note: NVIDIA is HUMAIN's founding GPU supplier: 18,000 GB300 in the first phase, expanded in November 2025 to up to 600,000 NVIDIA GPUs over three years.
relationships.context:
NVIDIA's May 2025 release set a plan of up to 500 MW and 'several hundred thousand' GPUs over five years, starting with 18,000 GB300. In November 2025 HUMAIN expanded it to 'up to 600,000' GPUs over three years across Saudi Arabia and the United States, with xAI named as partner for the first 18,000-GPU cluster.

The US licence issued the same day covers the equivalent of up to 35,000 GB300 chips, so most of the Saudi-sited volume needs further licensing. HUMAIN's own NVIDIA cloud launched at 1.1 MW (Global Data Center Hub).

relationships.scale: flagship '500 MW+' facility; US$3B HUMAIN equity in xAI (now SpaceX shares)
relationships.via: GPU data centres designed, built and operated by HUMAIN; Grok deployed nationwide
relationships.note: xAI is the anchor user of a planned HUMAIN-built network of GPU data centres led by a '500 MW+' flagship, and HUMAIN invested US$3B in xAI's Series E.
relationships.context:
HUMAIN's 19 Nov 2025 release announced 'a landmark framework agreement with xAI' to jointly develop GPU data centres 'anchored by a flagship 500 MW+ facility', combining 'HUMAIN's low-cost value proposition in infrastructure design, construction, and operations with xAI's leadership in frontier AI systems'. No site, owner split or builder is disclosed. At LEAP 2026 the Saudi Communications Minister said the xAI expansion would start at 50 MW and grow to 500 MW.

On 18 Feb 2026 HUMAIN invested US$3B in xAI's Series E, and the holding converted into SpaceX shares after the merger. Two relationships at once: HUMAIN is a shareholder in xAI's parent and the landlord-operator for xAI's Saudi compute. This dossier types the commercial one.

relationships.scale: up to 50 MW in the AI Zone by 2028; up to 150,000 accelerators
relationships.via: AWS AI Zone (Trainium and NVIDIA), HUMAIN ONE and ALLaM on AWS
relationships.note: AWS and HUMAIN are building a Riyadh 'AI Zone' in which AWS deploys and manages the accelerators; AWS is described as HUMAIN's preferred AI partner.
relationships.context: The AI Zone was announced at over US$5B in May 2025. In November 2025 AWS was to 'deploy and manage up to 150,000' accelerators in Riyadh. At LEAP 2026 (1 Sep 2026) the plan was stated as up to 50 MW by 2028. HUMAIN ONE is sold on AWS Marketplace, and ALLaM is to be offered on Amazon Bedrock. In this zone the hyperscaler operates the compute, so the fit-out is AWS's own buying.

relationships.via: ALLaM on Microsoft Foundry; HUMAIN ONE bundled with Microsoft 365 Copilot; HUMAIN AI PC on Windows
relationships.note: Microsoft and HUMAIN signed a long-term strategic collaboration in August 2026 covering models, enterprise software, consulting and AI PCs.
relationships.context: The 26 Aug 2026 release covers ALLaM on Microsoft platforms and Microsoft forward-deployed engineers. At LEAP 2026 the partnership was extended to a HUMAIN ONE bundle with Microsoft 365 Copilot on Azure, targeting one million users across the Middle East and Africa, and a Windows-based HUMAIN AI PC. No data-centre capacity is part of the published scope.

relationships.note: G42 is the Gulf's other sovereign AI builder; the US approved both for up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips on the same day, and since July 2026 only G42 holds licence-free access.
relationships.context: US Commerce's 19 Nov 2025 statement authorised exports to 'G42 … and Humain', each for up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips under security and reporting conditions. On 10 Jul 2026 BIS moved the UAE to Country Group A:5 and listed G42 and Core42 as approved licence-free recipients; Saudi Arabia was not moved. SemiAnalysis's ClusterMAX 3.0 places G42's Core42 in its Participation Ribbon tier and lists HUMAIN as unavailable.

policyExposure.exposure: HUMAIN's only disclosed US authorisation allows it to 'purchase the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips (GB300s)', 'conditioned on … meeting rigorous security and reporting requirements', with BIS monitoring compliance. Its plans run to 600,000 NVIDIA GPUs over three years and 120,000 chips for the Together AI build. Saudi Arabia was not moved to Country Group A:5 when the UAE was (10 Jul 2026), so further Saudi-sited volume needs further licences. The humain-m3 model, built by the Chinese company MiniMax (Sep 2026), is a new China-linkage point for any review.

A government-to-government framework, signed by Secretary Rubio and Prince Faisal bin Farhan, covering 'supply of advanced semiconductors' and AI infrastructure. It is not a licence; HUMAIN's chip access still runs through case-by-case BIS authorisations.

policyExposure.regime: Saudi AI infrastructure policy (MCIT enablement agreement; 2026 Year of AI)
policyExposure.exposure: MCIT and HUMAIN signed an agreement to support 'development of AI data centers by strengthening coordination … with relevant government entities to facilitate the enablement and expansion of infrastructure projects'. HUMAIN's grid supply comes through a National Grid SA agreement signed the next day. Electricity pricing for HUMAIN's sites is not disclosed first-party.

policyExposure.regime: EU merger control (PIF–Aramco joint acquisition of HUMAIN)
policyExposure.exposure: The European Commission cleared the joint acquisition under the simplified procedure (Argaam, 23 Jul 2026). The 'joint acquisition' framing implies Aramco would hold joint-control rights, not only a passive stake; the transaction has not been announced as complete.

Fortune (9 Sep 2026) frames the turn to outside capital as PIF limiting its portfolio companies' draw on the sovereign; Alvarez & Marsal's Kurt Davis Jr calls a 2029 listing one that 'puts the company in front of public investors mid-construction'.

financials.commentary: HUMAIN reports no financial statements. Its record is counterparty filings (MIS, stc), partner releases and anonymous-source reporting on financing. Collection gap: revenue, operating capacity in MW, capex spent, PIF capital injected and the Aramco consideration are all unknown.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that HUMAIN is the owner and grid counterparty for its own capacity, but that on its first 250 MW the equipment buyer is its EPC contractor. Basis: MIS's filings describe engineering, procurement and construction 'carried out under work orders issued by HUMAIN' and approved by HUMAIN. National Grid SA contracted with HUMAIN for 'the AI data centers project in Riyadh'. MEED reports HUMAIN itself tendered the Al-Saad campus's 380/132/33 kV substations and 2,000 MVA bulk supply point. On partner-led capacity — DataVolt, AirTrunk, the AWS AI Zone — the partner builds and buys. Inference: a power-equipment vendor needs HUMAIN's design acceptance and MIS's purchase order; no vendor list is published. Indicator to watch: the first MIS work orders announced on Tadawul, and a construction award for Al-Saad's substations.

(High confidence) We assess that the gap between HUMAIN's targets and its energised capacity is about three orders of magnitude. Basis: the one operating figure is a 1.1 MW NVIDIA cloud, plus an AMD cluster of undisclosed size. The targets are 1.9 GW by 2030 and about 6 GW by 2034, and HUMAIN's own claim is 1 GW at Al-Saad in 2027 against a NYT figure of 250 MW by the start of 2027. SemiAnalysis could not obtain 'a login and a functioning cluster'. Indicator to watch: handover of the first MIS-built hall (its original 12-month contract ran from March 2026) and any Al-Saad energisation date.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that export licensing, not power, is the binding constraint on HUMAIN's Saudi-sited compute. Basis: the only disclosed US authorisation is up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips, against a 600,000-GPU plan and 120,000 chips promised to Together AI's build. The UAE was moved to Country Group A:5 on 10 Jul 2026 and Saudi Arabia was not. humain-m3, built by MiniMax, gives reviewers a China-linkage point. Indicator to watch: a second BIS authorisation for HUMAIN, or a Saudi move to A:5.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that HUMAIN's demand is partly funded by HUMAIN: two of its anchor tenants are its own investees, and its growth now depends on outside capital. Basis: US$3B into xAI before xAI's 500 MW+ framework; HUMAIN led Luma AI's US$900M round, and Luma took the AMD joint venture's first 100 MW (Reuters). Aramco Ventures, whose parent is taking a HUMAIN stake, led Together AI's round (RuntimeWire). Financing has moved to a non-binding NIF framework, a reported Goldman-arranged package, a pending BSF Capital fund and a 2029 IPO. Indicator to watch: a closed debt facility or a signed stc joint-venture agreement.

(Low confidence) We assess that HUMAIN has stated no position on 800 VDC or solid-state transformers, and that its buying style favours packaged, modular power equipment delivered through EPCs. Basis: no first-party or counterparty source names a power-equipment supplier or any DC-distribution choice. Its data centres are described as 'robotic, modular, and optimized for the lowest total cost of ownership', and its first build is a phased EPC under work orders. This is inference from absence and from stated philosophy. Indicator to watch: an equipment specification for the Al-Saad halls or the xAI flagship.
